## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of Gatekeeper policy design, basic Rego, and CI validation.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper, ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, Rego basics
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, image allowlists

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (conceptual)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8spodsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8SPodSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8spodsecurity
      # policy consolidated in real template
```
```yaml
# Constraint (conceptual)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8SPodSecurity
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
  parameters:
    allowList:
      - registry.example.com/*
```

- How would you audit Gatekeeper decisions historically?

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes practical policy design at scale, focusing on admission controls, RBAC hygiene, and network isolation in a multi-cloud Kubernetes environment. It tests how a candidate translates security requirements into Gatekeeper constraints and integrates them into CI.

## Key Concepts
- Open Policy Agent (OPA) Gatekeeper constraint templates
- Kubernetes security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privilege constraints
- RBAC hardening: disallow cluster-admin bindings, namespace-label exceptions
- NetworkPolicy defaults and whitelisting
- CI integration: manifest validation, test manifests, failing/passing samples

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: noPrivileged
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snopriv
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNoPriv
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8snopriv
      violation["privileged container"] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.privileged == true
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sNoPriv
metadata:
  name: no-privileged-containers
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test these policies locally against a sample manifest?
- How would you manage exceptions for ops-managed namespaces without weakening security?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes policy-as-code skills, Istio security posture, and CI/CD integration. It tests ability to craft minimal, verifiable manifests and to reason about runtime vs CI checks.

## Key Concepts

- Istio PeerAuthentication mtls: STRICT
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno policy or alternative
- CI validation: lint, dry-run apply, policy testing
- Runtime enforcement: Istio sidecars enforce mTLS

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8smtlstrict
spec:
  crd:
    Spec:
      groups: ["constraints.gatekeeper.sh"]
      names:
        kind: K8sMTLSStrict
        plural: k8smTLSStricts
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8smtlstrict
        violation["mtls_missing"] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Namespace"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["istio-injection"]
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sMTLSStrict
metadata:
  name: mtls-strict
spec:
  match:
    requiredImages: []
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest: PeerAuthentication with mtls: STRICT
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: default
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest: missing PeerAuthentication
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample
  namespace: test
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you enable gradual rollout for mTLS enforcement?
- What exceptions would you permit and how would you audit them?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce cross-cloud data provenance and model lineage for ML workloads; ensures reproducibility and auditing of deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- Image digests, internal registries, provenance annotations
- MLflow tracking integration and run_id propagation
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Fail
  rules:
  - name: require-provenance-annotations
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Missing provenance annotations: model_version, dataset_hash, training_run_id'
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            model_version: '*'
            dataset_hash: '*'
            training_run_id: '*'
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Container image must include a digest'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@*'
```

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-fail
  annotations:
    model_version: v1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor:latest
```

```yaml

  name: ml-inference-pass

  replicas: 1
  template:

      labels:
        app: ml
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of namespace isolation and basic egress filtering using NetworkPolicy. It checks hands-on ability to craft minimal, enforceable rules and verify them.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics
- Namespace-scoped isolation
- Egress rules and default deny
- Basic verification via kubectl and logs

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-egress-isolate
  namespace: test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.2.3/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
        except:
        - 255.255.255.255/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod in test namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: test
```

## Why This Is Asked

- YAML manifest parsing

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```

## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up
- Extend to handle missing tests per service gracefully
- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Checks for API deprecation are common, and beginner-friendly gates show practical CI thinking without complex tooling.

## Key Concepts

- K8s API version deprecations
- CI gates in GitHub Actions
- Simple shell scripting for manifest checks
- Local verification versus PR gating

## Code Example

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
for f in k8s/**/*.yaml; do
  if grep -E \"apiVersion:\s*(extensions/v1beta1|apps/v1beta1|networking.k8s.io/v1beta1)\" \"$f\" >/dev/null; then
    echo \"Deprecated apiVersion found in $f\"
    exit 1
  fi
done
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to validate apiVersion per Kind map?
- How would you automatically fix or suggest updates and handle non-YAML files?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design real-time security boundaries between tenants, integrates runtime detection with policy, and automates containment. It also probes multi-cloud considerations, alerting, and mitigations.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime security tooling (Falco, OPA Gatekeeper)
- Kubernetes isolation (taints, labels, quarantine)
- CI/CD verification and incident response

## Code Example

```javascript
// Falco rule snippet (pseudo)
{
  "rule": "DENY_FORBIDDEN_RUNTIME",
  "condition": "evt.file.path in [\"/etc/shadow\",\"/etc/passwd\"] || container.privileged == true || evt.hostNetwork == true || net.egress > 0",
  "output": "FORBIDDEN_RUNTIME: container=%container.name user=%proc.name path=%evt.file.path",
  "priority": "CRITICAL"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the end-to-end in CI and in prod with canary workloads?
- What observability would you add to quickly diagnose false positives and tune rules?
